s: In many big cities, young people are choosing micro-apartments of less than twenty-five square meters.
Rents for these tiny homes are lower, and they are usually close to the city center.
paragraphs.zh: 在許多大城市，年輕人選擇不到二十五平方公尺的微型公寓。這種小房子房租較低，而且通常靠近市中心。

s: Supporters argue that owning fewer things makes life simpler.
Built-in furniture, such as beds that fold into the wall, saves surprising amounts of space.
paragraphs.zh: 支持者認為，擁有的東西越少，生活就越簡單。內建家具，例如可以收進牆裡的床，能省下驚人的空間。

s: Critics, however, warn that such small spaces can affect mental health, especially for people working from home.
Having no separate room to relax in, some residents say they feel trapped.
paragraphs.zh: 不過批評者警告，這麼小的空間可能影響心理健康，對在家工作的人尤其如此。因為沒有獨立的房間可以放鬆，有些住戶說自己覺得被困住了。

s: Most experts agree that micro-apartments work best as a short-term solution, rather than a home for life.
paragraphs.zh: 大多數專家都同意，微型公寓最適合當作短期的解決辦法，而不是一輩子的家。

s: Insects are eaten by around two billion people worldwide, yet in Europe and North America they are still considered strange.
This may be about to change.
paragraphs.zh: 全世界約有二十億人吃昆蟲，但在歐洲和北美，昆蟲仍被視為奇怪的食物。這種情況可能即將改變。

s: Producing insect protein requires far less land and water than raising cattle.
Crickets, for example, need about twelve times less food than cows to produce the same amount of protein.
paragraphs.zh: 生產昆蟲蛋白質所需的土地和水，遠比養牛少。舉例來說，要產出同樣多的蛋白質，蟋蟀需要的飼料大約只有牛的十二分之一。

s: Despite these benefits, many consumers find the idea disgusting.
Companies have therefore started grinding insects into flour, which can be used in bread or pasta without being noticed.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有這些好處，許多消費者還是覺得噁心。因此有些公司開始把昆蟲磨成粉，加進麵包或義大利麵裡，吃的人根本察覺不到。

s: Whether insects become a normal part of our diet will depend largely on price and taste.
paragraphs.zh: 昆蟲會不會成為我們日常飲食的一部分，主要取決於價格和味道。

s: Every summer, popular destinations such as Venice and Barcelona receive millions of visitors.
While tourism brings money and jobs, many locals feel that their cities are no longer their own.
paragraphs.zh: 每年夏天，像威尼斯和巴塞隆納這樣的熱門地點都會湧入數百萬遊客。觀光雖然帶來了錢和工作機會，但許多當地人覺得自己的城市已經不屬於自己了。

s: Rents have risen sharply, as apartments are increasingly rented to tourists instead of residents.
Traditional shops have been replaced by souvenir stores.
paragraphs.zh: 因為公寓越來越常租給觀光客而不是居民，房租急遽上漲。傳統商店也被紀念品店取代了。

s: Some cities have introduced measures to limit the crowds.
Venice now charges day visitors an entrance fee, while Amsterdam has stopped advertising itself abroad.
paragraphs.zh: 有些城市已經採取措施限制人潮。威尼斯現在向當日來回的遊客收取入城費，阿姆斯特丹則停止在國外宣傳自己。

s: Experts suggest that travelers can help by visiting in the off-season and exploring less famous places.
paragraphs.zh: 專家建議，旅客可以在淡季前往、多去探索較不知名的地方，來幫上一點忙。

s: Last September, after three days of heavy rain, the river in our small town rose by four meters in a single night.
Hundreds of homes were flooded.
paragraphs.zh: 去年九月，連下了三天大雨之後，我們小鎮的河水一夜之間上漲了四公尺。好幾百戶人家淹水了。

s: Fortunately, nobody was killed.
Thanks to a new warning system, residents received text messages hours before the water arrived.
Many managed to move their cars and valuables to higher ground.
paragraphs.zh: 幸好沒有人喪命。多虧了新的警報系統，居民在大水來臨前好幾個小時就收到了簡訊。很多人來得及把車子和貴重物品移到地勢較高的地方。

s: Scientists say floods like this are becoming more frequent as the climate gets warmer.
Concrete riverbanks, built decades ago, also make the water flow faster.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家說，隨著氣候變暖，這樣的洪水會越來越頻繁。幾十年前蓋的水泥河岸，也讓河水流得更快。

s: The town now plans to turn farmland along the river into wetlands, which can absorb large amounts of water.
paragraphs.zh: 鎮上現在計畫把河邊的農地改成濕地，因為濕地能吸收大量的水。

glossary.en: to cover with water; a lot of water on land

s: Have you ever thrown away a phone just because its battery died?
Many people have, since replacing the battery is often difficult or expensive.
paragraphs.zh: 你有沒有只因為電池壞了就把手機丟掉？很多人都這樣做過，因為換電池往往很麻煩或很貴。

s: Under new European rules, manufacturers will have to make products easier to repair.
Spare parts must be available for several years, and batteries must be replaceable by the user.
paragraphs.zh: 根據歐洲的新規定，製造商必須讓產品更容易維修。備用零件必須供應好幾年，電池也必須能讓使用者自行更換。

s: Supporters believe the law will reduce electronic waste, which is growing faster than any other kind of trash.
Some companies, however, claim that the changes will make devices thicker and more expensive.
paragraphs.zh: 支持者相信這項法律能減少電子垃圾，而電子垃圾正以比其他任何垃圾都快的速度增加。不過有些公司聲稱，這些改變會讓裝置變得更厚、更貴。

s: Either way, repairing rather than replacing is likely to become the norm.
paragraphs.zh: 無論如何，修理而不是換新，很可能會成為常態。

able to be bought or used

s: Research suggests that teenagers' body clocks shift during puberty, making it hard for them to fall asleep before eleven.
Yet many schools start before eight.
paragraphs.zh: 研究顯示，青少年在青春期時生理時鐘會往後移，讓他們很難在十一點前睡著。可是許多學校八點前就開始上課。

s: When several American schools moved their start time to half past eight, the results were impressive.
Students slept longer, were late less often and achieved better grades.
paragraphs.zh: 當幾所美國學校把上課時間延到八點半，結果令人印象深刻。學生睡得更久，遲到的次數變少，成績也進步了。

s: Not everyone is convinced, though.
Parents who work early worry about who will take their children to school.
Others point out that later finishing times leave less time for sports and part-time jobs.
paragraphs.zh: 不過，並不是每個人都被說服了。早上要上班的家長擔心誰來送孩子上學。也有人指出，放學時間延後會讓運動和打工的時間變少。

s: The debate is likely to continue for some time.
paragraphs.zh: 這場爭論很可能還會持續一段時間。

glossary.en: the time when a child's body becomes adult

mcq.zh: 生理時鐘往後移，很難早睡。
mcq.en: They shift, making it hard to sleep before eleven.

mcq.q: When did the American schools start after the change?
mcq.zh: 延到八點半。

mcq.q: Which result is mentioned?

mcq.en: Less time for sports and part-time jobs.

tf.s: Many schools start before eight.
Students at the later schools were late more often.
tf.en: False: they were late less often.

tf.s: Everyone agrees that schools should start later.

s: In 2020, Luxembourg became the first country in the world to make all public transport free.
Buses, trams and trains can be used without a ticket.
paragraphs.zh: 二〇二〇年，盧森堡成為全世界第一個讓所有大眾運輸都免費的國家。公車、電車和火車都不用買票就能搭。

s: The government hoped that fewer people would drive, reducing traffic jams and pollution.
The results, however, have been mixed.
paragraphs.zh: 政府希望開車的人會變少，從而減少塞車和污染。不過結果好壞參半。

s: Although the number of passengers has increased, most of them used to walk or cycle rather than drive.
Many commuters from neighboring countries still come by car because connections are poor.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然乘客人數增加了，但他們大多是原本走路或騎腳踏車的人，而不是開車的人。很多從鄰國來通勤的人還是開車，因為轉乘銜接很差。

s: Experts conclude that free tickets alone are not enough; services must also be fast and frequent.
paragraphs.zh: 專家的結論是：光是免費還不夠，班次也必須又快又密集。

s: Loneliness is often seen as a problem of old age, but surveys show that young adults report feeling lonely just as often.
Doctors are now treating it as a serious health issue.
paragraphs.zh: 孤獨常被當作老年人的問題，但調查顯示，年輕人感到孤獨的頻率其實一樣高。醫生現在把它當成嚴重的健康問題來看待。

s: Studies suggest that long-term loneliness can be as harmful as smoking fifteen cigarettes a day.
It increases the risk of heart disease and depression.
paragraphs.zh: 研究顯示，長期的孤獨可能和每天抽十五根菸一樣有害。它會提高心臟病和憂鬱症的風險。

s: In the United Kingdom, some doctors now prescribe social activities instead of medicine.
Patients might be sent to a gardening group, a choir or a walking club.
paragraphs.zh: 在英國，有些醫生現在會開「社交活動」而不是藥物的處方。病人可能會被轉介去參加園藝團體、合唱團或健走社。

s: Early results are encouraging, with many patients visiting their doctor less often.
paragraphs.zh: 初步結果令人鼓舞，許多病人看醫生的次數變少了。

They are lonelier than ever before

mcq.en: They report feeling lonely just as often.

mcq.q: Long-term loneliness can be as harmful as what?

mcq.q: Which activity is NOT mentioned?

mcq.q: What are the early results?

mcq.zh: 病人看醫生的次數變少。
mcq.en: Patients visit their doctor less often.

巧克力有一段悠久又迷人的歷史。古代中美洲的人用可可豆做成一種苦味的飲料，他們相信它有神奇的力量。十六世紀這種飲料傳到歐洲後，很快就在有錢人之間流行起來。不過很長一段時間裡，巧克力一直是飲料；直到十九世紀，才有人發明了做出固體巧克力的方法。今天巧克力到處買得到，而且受歡迎的程度絲毫沒有下降。有些科學家甚至說黑巧克力對健康有益，但也有人警告，吃太多顯然不健康。

items.text:
My first day as a reporter
I had imagined my first day at the Evening Post many times. In my imagination I was given an important story on my first morning, and by lunchtime the editor was congratulating me on my brilliant writing. The reality was rather different.
I arrived twenty minutes early, wearing a new suit that was slightly too big for me. The receptionist looked at me as if I had come to the wrong building. 'The newsroom's on the third floor,' she said eventually, 'but nobody will be there yet.' She was right. For half an hour I sat alone among the empty desks, reading yesterday's paper and trying to look busy.
When the editor, Margaret Hughes, finally arrived, she did not seem to have been expecting me. 'Ah, the new trainee,' she said, as though she had only just remembered I existed. She handed me a list of phone numbers. 'Call these people and ask if they've seen anything unusual this week. If anyone says yes, come and tell me.'
I spent the whole morning on the phone. Most people were polite but had seen nothing; a few were annoyed to be disturbed. Then, just before one o'clock, a woman told me that a large bird had been living on the roof of the town library for three days. It sounded far too small to be news, but I wrote it down anyway.
To my surprise, Margaret was delighted. 'That's exactly the kind of thing our readers love,' she said. By the evening I was standing outside the library with a photographer, watching an enormous eagle that had escaped from a nearby wildlife park. It wasn't the story I had imagined, but it was on the front page the next day, with my name underneath.

tr.zh:
我當記者的第一天
我想像過很多次在《晚報》上班的第一天：第一個早上就拿到重要的新聞，到中午總編輯已經在稱讚我文筆出色。現實卻大不相同。
我提早二十分鐘到，穿著一套稍微太大的新西裝。櫃台小姐看我的樣子，好像我走錯了大樓。「新聞部在三樓，」她終於開口，「不過現在還沒人。」她說得沒錯。半個小時裡，我一個人坐在空蕩蕩的辦公桌之間，看著昨天的報紙，努力裝得很忙。
總編輯瑪格麗特·休斯終於來了，看起來並沒在等我。「啊，新來的實習生，」她說，好像剛剛才想起有我這個人。她遞給我一張電話號碼表：「打給這些人，問他們這週有沒有看到什麼不尋常的事。如果有人說有，就來告訴我。」
我整個上午都在打電話。大部分人很客氣，但什麼也沒看到；有幾個人被打擾還不太高興。接著，快一點的時候，一位女士告訴我，有一隻大鳥在鎮立圖書館的屋頂上住了三天。這聽起來小到根本算不上新聞，但我還是記了下來。
出乎意料，瑪格麗特非常高興：「這正是讀者喜歡的那種事。」到了晚上，我和一位攝影師站在圖書館外，看著一隻從附近野生動物園逃出來的巨大老鷹。這不是我想像中的新聞，但第二天它登上了頭版，下面署著我的名字。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about his expectations in the first paragraph?
questions.zh: 他想像第一天就拿到重要新聞、中午就被稱讚，「現實卻大不相同」：期望不切實際。
questions.en: He imagined instant success; "the reality was rather different".

She took him to the newsroom.
She told him he was late.

questions.q: How did he feel about the woman's information?
options: He doubted it was important enough.
He was sure it would be on the front page.
He thought she was not telling the truth.
He was annoyed that she had called.

The eagle flew back to the park.
He was given a different story.

items.text:
Running my first marathon
Two years ago I could barely run for a bus. Last month I finished the London Marathon. (37) ＿＿＿＿＿ It started with a bet. A colleague said I would never manage to run five kilometres, so I signed up for a local fun run to prove him wrong.
The first few weeks of training were miserable. (38) ＿＿＿＿＿ My legs ached, I was always out of breath, and I seriously considered giving up.
Things changed when I joined a running club. (39) ＿＿＿＿＿ Running with other people made a huge difference, partly because we encouraged each other and partly because I didn't want to be the one who stopped first.
By the following spring I had completed a half marathon, and someone suggested I should try the full distance. (40) ＿＿＿＿＿ But once the idea was in my head, I couldn't forget it.
Training for a marathon takes over your life. (41) ＿＿＿＿＿ My weekends disappeared into long runs, and I had to say no to a lot of parties.
On the day itself, the crowds were incredible. (42) ＿＿＿＿＿ When I finally crossed the finish line, after four and a half hours, I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.
bank: I laughed at first, because it seemed completely impossible.
Strangers shouted my name, which I'd written on my shirt, and it kept me going.
I still can't quite believe it.
I went out three times a week, but I never seemed to get any faster.
For four months, I ran five or six times a week.
The members were friendly, and nobody cared how slow I was.
My colleague was the first to congratulate me on finishing the fun run.

tr.zh:
我的第一場馬拉松
兩年前，我連追公車都跑不動。上個月，我跑完了倫敦馬拉松。我到現在還不太敢相信。這一切始於一個打賭：一位同事說我連五公里都跑不完，所以我報名了當地的趣味路跑，想證明他錯了。
剛開始訓練的幾個星期很痛苦。我一週跑三次，卻好像怎麼也跑不快。腿痠、老是喘不過氣，我認真考慮過放棄。
加入跑步社以後，情況變了。社員都很友善，沒有人在意我跑得多慢。和別人一起跑差別很大，一方面我們互相打氣，一方面我也不想當第一個停下來的人。
到了隔年春天，我跑完了一場半馬，有人建議我試試全馬。一開始我笑了，因為那看起來完全不可能。可是這個念頭一進到腦子裡，就再也忘不掉。
準備馬拉松會佔據你的生活。四個月裡，我每週跑五、六次。週末都消失在長跑裡，很多派對也只好推掉。
比賽當天，觀眾多得驚人。陌生人喊著我寫在衣服上的名字，讓我撐了下去。花了四個半小時終於跨過終點線時，我不知道該笑還是該哭。

questions.zh: 前面說跑完了倫敦馬拉松，接著「我到現在還不太敢相信」。
questions.en: After finishing the marathon: "I still can't quite believe it."

questions.zh: 訓練很痛苦：一週跑三次卻跑不快，接著說腿痠、想放棄。
questions.en: Miserable training: no faster, aching legs.

questions.zh: 加入跑步社：社員很友善，接著說和別人一起跑差別很大。
questions.en: The club: friendly members, running together helped.

questions.zh: 有人建議跑全馬，他「一開始笑了」；後面的 But 說念頭還是忘不掉。
questions.en: He laughed at first — "But" the idea stayed.

questions.zh: 準備馬拉松佔據生活：四個月每週跑五、六次，週末都在長跑。
questions.en: Training took over: five or six runs a week.

questions.zh: 觀眾很多：陌生人喊他的名字讓他撐下去。G（同事恭喜他跑完趣味路跑）放哪裡都不合，是多出來的。
questions.en: The crowds shouted his name. G is the extra sentence.

bank: Lily, 19 — I started selling handmade jewellery online when I was sixteen. My parents weren't convinced it was a good idea; they thought I should be concentrating on my exams. Now I have three people working for me. My advice? Listen to your customers. Every new design I make starts with something a customer has asked for.

Omar, 22 — At university I was shocked by how much textbooks cost, so I created an app for students to swap them. My first version was a disaster — nobody could work out how to use it — and I nearly gave up. Luckily an investor saw the second version and offered to support me.

Grace, 24 — I opened a vegan bakery with money I borrowed from my grandmother. I start at four in the morning and rarely finish before eight in the evening, but I love it. Next year I'm hoping to open a second shop on the other side of the city.

Ben, 21 — I repair old bikes and sell them again, mainly because I hate seeing things thrown away when they could still be used. I work from my parents' garage, and on Saturdays I run workshops where I teach people to fix their own bikes.

tr.zh:
A 莉莉（19 歲）：我十六歲開始在網路上賣手工飾品。爸媽一開始不太看好，覺得我應該專心準備考試。現在我有三個員工。我的建議是：聽客人的話。我每一個新設計都是從客人的要求開始的。
B 奧馬（22 歲）：大學時我被課本的價格嚇到，所以做了一個讓學生交換課本的應用程式。第一版很失敗，沒人搞得懂怎麼用，我差點放棄。幸好有一位投資人看到第二版，願意支持我。
C 葛蕾絲（24 歲）：我向奶奶借錢開了一家純素烘焙坊。我凌晨四點開工，很少晚上八點前收工，但我很喜歡。明年我希望在城市的另一頭開第二家店。
D 班（21 歲）：我修理舊腳踏車再賣出去，主要是因為我討厭看到還能用的東西被丟掉。我在爸媽的車庫工作，每個星期六開工作坊，教大家自己修車。

items.text:
City bees
Beekeeping has (1) ＿＿＿＿＿ off in cities in recent years. Hives can now be found on the roofs of offices, hotels and even famous museums. City bees often (2) ＿＿＿＿＿ better than their country cousins, because parks and gardens offer a wide (3) ＿＿＿＿＿ of flowers, while farmland may contain only one crop. However, experts warn that the trend may have gone too far. In some areas there are now so many hives that there is not (4) ＿＿＿＿＿ food for all the bees, and wild bees are (5) ＿＿＿＿＿ out. Beekeepers are therefore being (6) ＿＿＿＿＿ to plant more flowers before adding new hives. As one scientist (7) ＿＿＿＿＿ it, 'Keeping bees is not the same as saving them.' Anyone thinking of starting should (8) ＿＿＿＿＿ advice from a local beekeeping club first.

tr.zh:
城市裡的蜜蜂
近年來，養蜂在城市裡流行起來。現在辦公大樓、飯店，甚至知名博物館的屋頂上都看得到蜂箱。城市的蜜蜂常常比鄉下的同類過得好，因為公園和花園有各式各樣的花，農地卻可能只種一種作物。不過專家警告，這股風潮可能過頭了。有些地區蜂箱多到食物不夠所有蜜蜂吃，野生蜜蜂因此吃虧。所以養蜂人被呼籲先多種花，再增加新蜂箱。就像一位科學家說的：「養蜜蜂不等於拯救蜜蜂。」想開始養蜂的人，最好先向當地的養蜂社請教。

questions.zh: 「take off」：（事物）開始流行、起飛。
「do better」：過得更好、表現更好。
「a wide range of」：各式各樣的。
「not enough food」：食物不夠；plenty / lots 要加 of。
questions.en: not enough food; plenty and lots need "of".

questions.zh: 「lose out」：吃虧、處於不利。
questions.en: lose out = be at a disadvantage.

questions.zh: 「be urged to do」：被呼籲做某事；insist / demand / suggest 不能用「人 + to do」。
questions.en: urged to plant; the others do not take "someone to do".

questions.zh: 「As one scientist puts it」：就像一位科學家說的。
「seek advice」：徵求建議。

items.text:
Taking a short nap
In many countries, sleeping during the day is seen as a sign of laziness. (9) ＿＿＿＿＿, research suggests that a short afternoon nap can actually make us more productive. A sleep of (10) ＿＿＿＿＿ more than twenty minutes can improve memory and concentration (11) ＿＿＿＿＿ leaving us feeling tired afterwards. Sleeping for longer, on the other hand, can make it harder to wake (12) ＿＿＿＿＿ properly. Some companies have even set up special rooms (13) ＿＿＿＿＿ employees can rest during their lunch break. Not everyone is convinced, (14) ＿＿＿＿＿. Critics argue that if people need to sleep at work, it is because they are not getting enough sleep at night. (15) ＿＿＿＿＿ the case, a short rest is certainly better (16) ＿＿＿＿＿ a third cup of coffee.

tr.zh:
小睡片刻
在很多國家，白天睡覺被看成懶惰的表現。不過研究顯示，下午短暫小睡其實能讓我們更有效率。睡不超過二十分鐘，就能改善記憶力和專注力，醒來也不會覺得累。相反地，睡太久反而更難完全清醒。有些公司甚至設了專門的房間，讓員工午休時休息。不過並不是每個人都認同。批評者認為，如果人需要在上班時睡覺，那是因為晚上睡得不夠。無論如何，短暫休息肯定比第三杯咖啡好。

questions.zh: 前一句說午睡被當成懶惰，接著說研究顯示午睡有好處：轉折用 However。
「no more than twenty minutes」：不超過二十分鐘。
「without leaving us feeling tired」：不會讓我們覺得累。
「wake up」：醒來。
「rooms where employees can rest」：指地點的關係副詞 where。
句尾的「though / however」：不過。
「Whatever the case」：無論如何。
「better than」：比……好。

items.text:
Working holidays
Each year, thousands of young people spend their summer (17) ＿＿＿＿＿ (VOLUNTEER) on projects abroad, from building schools to protecting turtles. For many, it is an (18) ＿＿＿＿＿ (FORGET) experience. However, some organisations have been criticised for charging (19) ＿＿＿＿＿ (REASON) high fees, while the work itself is not always (20) ＿＿＿＿＿ (EFFECT). Before signing up, it is (21) ＿＿＿＿＿ (ADVICE) to find out exactly where your money goes. A good organisation will be happy to provide this (22) ＿＿＿＿＿ (INFORM). It is also worth asking about the (23) ＿＿＿＿＿ (QUALIFY) of the people who will supervise you. Above all, remember that the most (24) ＿＿＿＿＿ (SUCCEED) projects are those planned together with the local community.

tr.zh:
海外志工假期
每年都有成千上萬的年輕人，利用暑假到國外參加志工計畫，從蓋學校到保護海龜都有。對很多人來說，那是難忘的經驗。不過，有些機構因為收費高得不合理而受到批評，而工作本身也不一定有成效。報名之前，最好先弄清楚你的錢到底用在哪裡。好的機構會很樂意提供這些資訊。也值得問問負責督導你的人有什麼資格。最重要的是記住：最成功的計畫，都是和當地社區一起規劃的。

questions.zh: spend time + V-ing：「spend their summer volunteering」。
FORGET → unforgettable：難忘的（un- + -able）。
修飾形容詞 high 要用副詞，而且是「不合理地」高：unreasonably。
EFFECT → effective：有成效的（be 動詞後用形容詞）。
ADVICE → advisable：「it is advisable to …」最好……
INFORM → information（名詞，this information）。
QUALIFY → qualifications：資格（the … of，複數）。
SUCCEED → successful：最成功的（the most + 形容詞）。

(30) 他三年前開始學日文。→ He ___ Japanese for three years.（BEEN）

questions.zh: 對過去的肯定否定推測：「can't have + 過去分詞」不可能拿了。
questions.en: can't have taken — certain it didn't happen.

questions.zh: 沒人比我高 = 我是班上最高的：am the tallest。
未來式被動：will be + 過去分詞。
「Would you mind + V-ing」：請你……好嗎？
與過去事實相反的條件句：if + had + 過去分詞。
questions.en: if I hadn't been — third conditional.

questions.zh: 從過去持續到現在：現在完成進行式 has been learning。
questions.en: has been learning — still going on.

items.text:
The summer I worked in a bookshop
When I was seventeen, I was desperate for a summer job, but every café and clothes shop in town had already taken on students. In the end, the only place that would have me was Hargreaves Books, a dusty second-hand bookshop that most people walked past without noticing. I accepted the job without enthusiasm, assuming I would spend two months bored out of my mind.
Mr Hargreaves himself did little to change my mind on the first day. He was a tall, silent man in his seventies who seemed to communicate mainly by pointing. He pointed at the shelves that needed dusting, at the boxes that needed unpacking and, at five o'clock, at the door. I went home convinced I had made a terrible mistake.
Things began to change in my second week, when a customer asked for a book I had never heard of. Before I could apologise, Mr Hargreaves appeared beside me, walked straight to a shelf at the back of the shop and took down the very copy she wanted. 'Every book in here,' he told me afterwards, 'is somewhere for a reason.' It was the longest sentence he had spoken to me.
From then on, he began to explain his system — if 'system' is the right word. Books were not arranged by author or subject, but according to connections that only he understood: a novel about the sea beside a cookery book from Portugal, a history of clocks next to a collection of poems about time. At first I found it maddening. By August, I could find almost anything.
On my last day, Mr Hargreaves handed me a parcel wrapped in brown paper. Inside was a book I had picked up dozens of times but never bought, because I couldn't afford it. Inside the cover he had written: 'For the only assistant who ever learnt where things are.' I still have it on my desk.

tr.zh:
我在書店打工的那個夏天
我十七歲時非常想找暑期工作，可是鎮上每家咖啡店、服飾店都已經找好學生了。最後唯一肯用我的，是哈格里夫斯書店，一家灰撲撲的二手書店，大多數人經過都不會注意到。我勉強接下這份工作，以為接下來兩個月會無聊得要命。
第一天，哈格里夫斯先生本人也沒讓我改觀。他是七十多歲、又高又沉默的男人，好像主要靠用手指來溝通。他指著要撢灰的書架、要拆的箱子，五點鐘時指著門。我回家時深信自己犯了大錯。
第二週情況開始改變。有位客人要找一本我聽都沒聽過的書。我還來不及道歉，哈格里夫斯先生就出現在我旁邊，直接走到書店後面的一個書架，拿下了她要的那一本。「這裡的每一本書，」他事後對我說，「放在哪裡都有原因。」那是他對我說過最長的一句話。
從那之後，他開始向我解釋他的系統——如果那算得上系統的話。書不是照作者或主題排，而是照只有他懂的關聯：一本關於大海的小說旁邊放葡萄牙的食譜，一本時鐘史旁邊放一本關於時間的詩集。一開始我快被逼瘋了。到了八月，我幾乎什麼都找得到。
最後一天，哈格里夫斯先生遞給我一個用牛皮紙包著的包裹。裡面是一本我拿起來看過幾十次、卻因為買不起而從沒買的書。封面內頁他寫著：「給唯一學會東西放在哪裡的店員。」那本書到現在還在我的書桌上。

questions.q: Why did the writer take the job at the bookshop?
options: He had always loved old books.
It paid better than a café.
questions.zh: 其他店都找好學生了，「唯一肯用我的」就是這家書店。
questions.en: It was the only place that would have him.

questions.q: What was the writer's impression of Mr Hargreaves on the first day?
options: He did not want an assistant.
questions.zh: 「又高又沉默」，主要靠用手指溝通。

questions.q: What surprised the writer in his second week?
options: how quickly Mr Hargreaves found a book
questions.zh: 老闆「直接走到」書架，拿下客人要的那一本。
questions.en: Mr Hargreaves went straight to the right book.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest with the words 'if "system" is the right word'?
options: The books were not in the usual order.
questions.zh: 書不按作者或主題排，而是照老闆自己的關聯。
questions.en: Not by author or subject, but by his own links.

questions.q: How did the writer feel about the arrangement at first?
questions.zh: 「一開始我快被逼瘋了」（maddening）：很挫折。

questions.q: What does the final paragraph show?
options: The writer bought the book with his wages.
Mr Hargreaves had noticed which book the writer liked.
Mr Hargreaves wanted him to stay.
questions.zh: 送他的正是他「拿起來看過幾十次」卻買不起的書：老闆注意到了。
questions.en: The gift was the book he had picked up dozens of times.

items.text:
Living without a car
Three years ago, my husband and I sold our car. It wasn't an easy decision. (37) ＿＿＿＿＿ But the car was costing us a fortune, and we were using it less and less.
The first few weeks were a challenge. Shopping, in particular, needed a complete rethink. (38) ＿＿＿＿＿ Now we buy smaller amounts more often, mostly from the shops within walking distance, and we waste far less food.
We had expected the children to complain, but they adapted faster than we did. (39) ＿＿＿＿＿ Our daughter, who is fourteen, says she likes being able to go where she wants without asking us for a lift.
There are, of course, times when we miss having a car. (40) ＿＿＿＿＿ On those occasions, we use a car-sharing scheme, which lets us rent a car by the hour from a street near our flat.
Perhaps the biggest change has been to our health. (41) ＿＿＿＿＿ Neither of us has been to the gym since we sold the car, and yet we are both fitter than we have been for years.
I'm not saying that everyone could live like this. (42) ＿＿＿＿＿ But for us, giving up the car has been one of the best decisions we've ever made.
bank: We both walk or cycle at least an hour a day without really thinking about it.
Visiting my parents, who live in a village with one bus a day, is the obvious example.
We had both been driving since we were teenagers.
We used to do one enormous trip to the supermarket every Saturday.
They soon discovered that the bus was more fun than the back seat.
People in the countryside, or with small children, may find it impossible.
The car was eventually sold to a neighbour.

tr.zh:
沒有車的生活
三年前，我和先生把車賣了。那不是容易的決定。我們兩個從青少年時期就開車了。可是那輛車花了我們好多錢，而且我們用得越來越少。
頭幾個星期很有挑戰。尤其是買東西，得整個重新想過。我們以前每個星期六都去超市大採購一次。現在我們少量多次地買，大多在走路就到的商店，浪費的食物也少多了。
我們本來以為孩子會抱怨，結果他們比我們還快適應。他們很快就發現搭公車比坐後座好玩。我們十四歲的女兒說，她喜歡想去哪就去哪，不用拜託我們載。
當然也有懷念有車的時候。去看我爸媽就是最明顯的例子，他們住的村子一天只有一班公車。遇到這種時候，我們就用共享汽車，在我們公寓附近的街上按小時租車。
也許最大的改變是我們的健康。我們兩個每天都會走路或騎車至少一小時，幾乎不用刻意去想。賣車之後我們都沒去過健身房，卻比這些年來任何時候都健康。
我不是說每個人都能這樣生活。住在鄉下或有小小孩的人，可能就做不到。但對我們來說，放棄開車是我們做過最好的決定之一。

questions.zh: 不容易的決定，因為「我們兩個從青少年時期就開車了」；後面的 But 接著說車太花錢。
questions.en: Driving since their teens — "But" the cost.

questions.zh: 買東西要重新想過：以前每週六大採購，對照後面的「現在」少量多次。
questions.en: One big Saturday shop before; smaller trips now.

questions.zh: 孩子比大人快適應：發現公車比坐後座好玩。
questions.en: The children found the bus more fun.

questions.zh: 懷念有車的時候：去看住在只有一班公車的村子的爸媽；後面 On those occasions 接著說租車。
questions.en: Visiting her parents — "on those occasions" they rent a car.

questions.zh: 健康的改變：每天走路或騎車一小時，接著說不用去健身房也更健康。
questions.en: An hour of walking or cycling a day.

questions.zh: 不是每個人都能這樣：鄉下或有小小孩的人可能做不到。G 放哪裡都不合，是多出來的。
questions.en: Some people could not do it. G is the extra sentence.

bank: Marco, 45 — I started Japanese when my company moved me to Osaka. I had lessons twice a week, but honestly I learnt most from my neighbours, an elderly couple who invited me for dinner every Friday. Reading is still a struggle — there are so many characters — but I can hold a conversation about almost anything now.

Hannah, 38 — I chose Spanish simply because I'd always loved the sound of it. I used an app every morning on the train for two years, but it was only when I spent a month in Mexico that I could actually speak. I was embarrassed to make mistakes at first, but people were so patient.

Raj, 52 — My daughter married a German man, and I wanted to be able to talk to his family. I'm not a natural language learner — I failed French at school — so I hired a private tutor. It's expensive, but I need someone to push me. Last Christmas I gave a short speech in German, and everybody cried.

Sofia, 41 — I got into Korean through TV dramas. At first I just wanted to understand them without subtitles, but then I became interested in the culture and history. I've joined an online group where learners practise together, and I've made friends all over the world. I'm planning my first trip to Seoul next spring.

tr.zh:
A 馬可（45 歲）：公司把我調到大阪，我才開始學日文。我一週上兩次課，不過老實說，我學最多的是從鄰居那裡，一對每個星期五都請我吃晚餐的老夫婦。閱讀還是很吃力，字太多了，但現在我幾乎什麼話題都能聊。
B 漢娜（38 歲）：我選西班牙文，只是因為一直很喜歡它的聲音。我兩年來每天早上在火車上用 App 學，但直到在墨西哥待了一個月，才真的開得了口。一開始我很怕說錯，可是大家都好有耐心。
C 拉吉（52 歲）：我女兒嫁給一個德國人，我想能和他的家人說話。我不是天生會學語言的人，在學校法文還被當過，所以我請了家教。很貴，但我需要有人督促我。去年聖誕節我用德文說了一段簡短的致詞，大家都哭了。
D 蘇菲亞（41 歲）：我是看韓劇開始學韓文的。一開始只是想不看字幕也能懂，後來開始對文化和歷史有興趣。我加入了一個學習者一起練習的線上社群，交到了世界各地的朋友。我正在計畫明年春天第一次去首爾。

questions.q: Which person learned mainly through people they met socially?
questions.zh: 馬可「學最多的是從鄰居那裡」，每週五一起吃晚餐。
questions.en: Marco learnt most from his neighbours.

questions.q: Which person felt uncomfortable about making mistakes?
questions.zh: 漢娜「一開始我很怕說錯」。
questions.en: Hannah was embarrassed to make mistakes.

questions.q: Which person was motivated by a family connection?
questions.zh: 拉吉的女兒嫁給德國人，他想和親家說話。
questions.en: Raj wanted to talk to his daughter's in-laws.

questions.q: Which person started learning because of entertainment?
questions.zh: 蘇菲亞「是看韓劇開始學韓文的」。

questions.q: Which person admits they found languages difficult in the past?
questions.zh: 拉吉「在學校法文還被當過」。

questions.q: Which person still finds one skill particularly hard?
questions.zh: 馬可「閱讀還是很吃力」。
questions.en: Reading is still a struggle for Marco.

questions.q: Which person has made international friendships through learning?
questions.zh: 蘇菲亞「交到了世界各地的朋友」。
questions.en: Sofia has friends all over the world.

questions.q: Which person made a breakthrough during a trip abroad?
questions.zh: 漢娜「直到在墨西哥待了一個月，才真的開得了口」。
questions.en: Hannah could speak after a month in Mexico.

questions.q: Which person pays for one-to-one lessons?
questions.zh: 拉吉「請了家教」，而且很貴。

questions.q: Which person has not yet visited the country whose language they are learning?
questions.zh: 蘇菲亞「正在計畫明年春天第一次去首爾」。
questions.en: Sofia is planning her first trip.

items.text:
Back in the groove
Twenty years ago, few people would have (1) ＿＿＿＿＿ that vinyl records would make a comeback. Music fans had (2) ＿＿＿＿＿ to CDs and then to downloads, and record shops were closing (3) ＿＿＿＿＿ the country. Yet sales of vinyl have risen every year for more than a decade. So what (4) ＿＿＿＿＿ for this surprising trend? Many buyers say they enjoy the (5) ＿＿＿＿＿ experience of owning music: the large artwork, the ritual of putting a record on, even the occasional crackle. Others simply like the way it sounds, (6) ＿＿＿＿＿ experts disagree about whether vinyl is really better. Interestingly, a large (7) ＿＿＿＿＿ of the people buying records are under thirty, and some of them do not even own a record player. For them, it seems, a record is (8) ＿＿＿＿＿ an object to display as a way to listen to music.

tr.zh:
黑膠回來了
二十年前，很少人會預料到黑膠唱片會捲土重來。樂迷先改用 CD，後來又改用下載，全國各地的唱片行一家家關門。然而十多年來，黑膠的銷量年年上升。這個令人意外的趨勢該怎麼解釋？很多買家說，他們喜歡擁有音樂的實體感受：大幅的封面藝術、放唱片的儀式感，甚至偶爾的劈啪聲。也有人就是喜歡它的聲音，雖然專家對黑膠是否真的比較好聽看法不一。有趣的是，買唱片的人有很大比例不到三十歲，其中有些人甚至沒有唱盤。對他們來說，唱片似乎既是拿來聽音樂的，也是拿來展示的物品。

questions.zh: 「few people would have predicted that …」：很少人會預料到。
「switch to」：改用；replace / exchange 後面不接 to 表示改用。
「across the country」：全國各地。
「account for」：解釋、說明原因；explain 不加 for。
「the physical experience」：實體的感受（拿在手上、放唱片）。
後面是完整子句 experts disagree…，要用連接詞 although；despite 後接名詞。
questions.en: although + clause; despite needs a noun.

questions.zh: 「a large proportion of the people」：很大比例的人；amount / quantity / deal 不用在人。
「as much A as B」：既是 A 也是 B。
questions.en: as much an object … as a way to listen.

items.text:
Why cats purr
Most people assume that cats purr because they are happy. While this is often true, it is not the (9) ＿＿＿＿＿ explanation. Cats also purr when they are frightened, injured or even giving birth. Some scientists believe that purring may (10) ＿＿＿＿＿ cats to heal: the vibrations are at frequencies that are known to strengthen bones. This could explain (11) ＿＿＿＿＿ cats seem to recover from injuries so quickly. Kittens begin purring when they are (12) ＿＿＿＿＿ a few days old, probably to let their mother know that all is well. Interestingly, some cats have learnt to use a special purr (13) ＿＿＿＿＿ they want food. This sound contains a cry (14) ＿＿＿＿＿ is similar to that of a human baby, which makes it very hard for owners to ignore. In other words, your cat may (15) ＿＿＿＿＿ be as innocent as it looks — it may be training you, (16) ＿＿＿＿＿ than the other way round!

tr.zh:
貓為什麼會呼嚕
大多數人以為貓呼嚕是因為開心。這雖然常常沒錯，卻不是唯一的解釋。貓在害怕、受傷甚至生產時也會呼嚕。有些科學家認為，呼嚕可能有助於貓療傷：這種振動的頻率已知能強化骨骼。這也許能解釋為什麼貓受傷後好像恢復得特別快。小貓出生才幾天就開始呼嚕，大概是要告訴媽媽一切都好。有趣的是，有些貓學會了在想要食物時，用一種特別的呼嚕聲。這種聲音裡夾著一種像人類嬰兒的哭聲，讓主人很難不理。換句話說，你的貓可能沒有看起來那麼無辜——可能是牠在訓練你，而不是你在訓練牠！

questions.zh: 「not the only explanation」：不是唯一的解釋。
「help / allow / enable cats to heal」：幫助貓療傷。
「explain why …」：解釋為什麼。
「only / just a few days old」：才幾天大。
「when they want food」：想要食物的時候。
「a cry that / which is similar to …」：關係代名詞指 cry。
「may not be as innocent as it looks」：可能沒有看起來那麼無辜。
「rather than the other way round」：而不是反過來。
questions.en: rather than the other way round.

items.text:
Living small
A growing number of people are choosing to live in 'tiny houses' — homes with an area of less than forty square metres. For some, the (17) ＿＿＿＿＿ (ATTRACT) is mainly financial: a tiny house costs (18) ＿＿＿＿＿ (CONSIDER) less than a normal home. Others are motivated by environmental (19) ＿＿＿＿＿ (AWARE). Living in a small space forces you to reduce your (20) ＿＿＿＿＿ (POSSESS) and use less energy. However, life in a tiny house is not without its (21) ＿＿＿＿＿ (DIFFICULT). Finding land can be (22) ＿＿＿＿＿ (SURPRISE) hard, and in many areas tiny houses are not (23) ＿＿＿＿＿ (OFFICE) allowed as permanent homes. Owners also admit that sharing such a small space can test even the strongest (24) ＿＿＿＿＿ (RELATE).

tr.zh:
住小一點
越來越多人選擇住在「迷你屋」，也就是面積不到四十平方公尺的房子。對有些人來說，吸引力主要在錢：迷你屋比一般房子便宜得多。也有人是出於環保意識。住在小空間會逼你減少家當，也用更少的能源。不過，住迷你屋也不是沒有困難。找土地可能出乎意料地難，而且很多地區並不正式允許把迷你屋當永久住所。屋主也承認，共享這麼小的空間，連最穩固的感情都會受到考驗。

questions.zh: ATTRACT → attraction（名詞，the …）：吸引力。
修飾 less 要用副詞：considerably less 便宜得多。
AWARE → awareness：意識（environmental awareness 環保意識）。
POSSESS → possessions：擁有的東西、家當（複數）。
DIFFICULT → difficulties（its + 名詞，複數）。
修飾形容詞 hard 用副詞：surprisingly hard 出乎意料地難。
OFFICE → officially：正式地（修飾 allowed）。
RELATE → relationships：感情、關係（the strongest + 複數名詞）。

items.text:
(25) 'Don't touch the paintings,' the guide told us.
      NOT
      The guide told us ＿＿＿＿＿ the paintings.
(26) It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.
      SO
      The film ＿＿＿＿＿ that I fell asleep.
(27) Someone stole my bike last night.
      HAD
      I ＿＿＿＿＿ last night.
(28) It's possible that Tom missed the train.
      MAY
      Tom ＿＿＿＿＿ the train.

tr.zh:
(25) 導覽員對我們說：「不要碰畫。」→ The guide told us ___ the paintings.（NOT）
(26) 那部電影無聊到我睡著了。→ The film ___ that I fell asleep.（SO）

(29) 雖然在下雨，我們還是去散步了。→ We went for a walk ___ was raining.（DESPITE）
(30) 我今晚比較想待在家。→ I ___ at home tonight.（RATHER）

questions.zh: 否定的命令轉成間接引語：told us not to + 原形動詞。
「so + 形容詞 + that」：如此……以致於。
「have something + 過去分詞」：（不好的事）發生在自己的東西上。
對過去的推測：may have + 過去分詞。
despite 後面不能直接接子句，要說「despite the fact (that) + 子句」。
questions.en: despite the fact (that) it was raining.

questions.zh: 「would rather + 原形動詞」：寧願、比較想。

items.text:
Why I gave up my phone for a month
It began as a joke. Over dinner, my sister bet me that I couldn't last a week without my smartphone. I was offended — I'm a journalist, not a teenager — and announced that I could manage a month. It was only on the way home, checking my messages for the tenth time that evening, that I began to suspect I might have made a mistake.
The first three days were genuinely uncomfortable. I kept reaching for my pocket, the way people who have lost a tooth keep touching the gap with their tongue. Without a map app, I got lost twice. Without a train timetable, I spent forty minutes on a cold platform. I also realised how often I had used the phone simply to avoid being bored: in queues, in waiting rooms, even during adverts on television.
By the second week, though, something had shifted. Boredom, I discovered, is not as painful as I had feared. On the bus I watched people, or looked out of the window, or simply thought. Ideas for articles came to me in a way they hadn't for years. I read three novels — more than I had read in the previous twelve months.
Not everything improved. Some friends found me harder to reach and stopped trying; I missed two parties because the invitations were sent by message. Work was more complicated too, since my editor expected instant replies. 'It's very admirable,' she said, in a tone that suggested it wasn't.
When the month ended, I switched the phone back on and watched hundreds of notifications arrive. I felt not relief but a kind of tiredness. I haven't gone back to how I was. The phone now lives in a drawer in the evenings, and the map app is the only one I've reinstalled without hesitation.

tr.zh:
我為什麼戒手機一個月
一開始只是開玩笑。吃晚餐時，我姊姊跟我打賭，說我沒辦法一週不用智慧型手機。我覺得被冒犯了——我是記者，又不是青少年——就宣布我能撐一個月。直到回家路上，那晚第十次查看訊息時，我才開始懷疑自己可能犯了錯。
頭三天真的很難受。我一直伸手去摸口袋，就像掉了牙的人一直用舌頭去碰那個缺口。沒有地圖 App，我迷路兩次。沒有火車時刻表，我在冷冰冰的月台上等了四十分鐘。我也發現自己有多常只是為了不無聊而拿手機：排隊時、在候診室，甚至看電視廣告時。
不過到了第二週，有些東西變了。我發現無聊並沒有我原本怕的那麼難受。在公車上，我看看人、看看窗外，或只是想事情。寫文章的點子以多年未有的方式冒出來。我看了三本小說，比過去十二個月看的還多。
也不是每件事都變好。有些朋友覺得我比較難聯絡，就不再找我了；有兩場派對因為邀請是用訊息傳的，我錯過了。工作也變得更複雜，因為我的主編期待立刻回覆。「真是令人佩服，」她說，語氣卻聽得出並非如此。
一個月結束後，我重新開機，看著幾百則通知湧進來。我感到的不是解脫，而是一種疲倦。我沒有回到以前的樣子。現在晚上手機都放在抽屜裡，地圖 App 是我唯一毫不猶豫重新安裝的。

The boat in the garden
When my father retired, he surprised us all by buying an old wooden sailing boat. It had been lying in a farmer's field for twenty years. (37) ＿＿＿＿＿ My mother asked, reasonably enough, where he intended to keep it. The answer turned out to be our back garden.
For the first year, the boat sat under a plastic sheet while Dad read every book he could find about wooden boats. (38) ＿＿＿＿＿ He has always believed in understanding a job completely before starting it.
The real work began the following spring. Much of the wood was rotten and had to be replaced, piece by piece, using traditional methods. (39) ＿＿＿＿＿ In the end, Dad found an elderly boat-builder in the next village who was happy to share his knowledge in exchange for company and cups of tea.
Progress was slow. There were months when nothing seemed to happen, and the neighbours began making jokes about it. (40) ＿＿＿＿＿ But Dad simply smiled and carried on.
Six years after he bought it, the boat was finally finished. (41) ＿＿＿＿＿ We hired a truck to take it to the coast, and half the street came to watch it leave.
Last summer Dad sailed it along the coast with my brother. (42) ＿＿＿＿＿ He says he's already looking for his next project, which is exactly what my mother was afraid of.
bank: This was a skill that very few people still had.
One of them asked whether he was building it for the next flood.
Its paint had gone and there were holes in the bottom.
It was the first time it had been on the water for over a quarter of a century.
It looked even more beautiful than any of us had imagined.
Not once did he pick up a tool.
It took him less than a week to finish the job.

tr.zh:
院子裡的船
我爸退休時買了一艘老木帆船，讓我們全都嚇一跳。那艘船在農夫的田裡躺了二十年。船漆都掉光了，船底還有破洞。我媽很合理地問他打算把船放哪裡。答案是我們家後院。
第一年，船蓋著塑膠布擺在那裡，爸爸則把找得到的木船書都讀了一遍。他連一次工具都沒拿起來過。他一向相信，開工前要先把一件事完全弄懂。
真正的工作從隔年春天開始。很多木頭都爛了，得用傳統方法一塊一塊換掉。這是一門已經很少人會的手藝。最後爸爸在隔壁村找到一位老造船師傅，他很樂意分享所學，只要有人陪他聊天、喝茶。
進度很慢。有好幾個月好像什麼進展都沒有，鄰居開始拿這件事開玩笑。有一個人問他是不是在為下一次大洪水造船。但爸爸只是笑笑，繼續做下去。
買船六年後，船終於完成了。它比我們任何人想像的都還要漂亮。我們租了一台卡車把船載到海邊，半條街的人都來看它離開。
去年夏天，爸爸和我哥開著它沿海岸航行。那是它二十五年多來第一次下水。他說他已經在找下一個計畫了——這正是我媽最怕的。

bank: Paul, 48 — I spent twenty years in banking and earned a lot of money, but I never felt I had made anything real. When my company cut jobs, I took the payment and trained as a carpenter. I earn far less now, and my family had to move to a smaller house, but I go to work every morning looking forward to it.

Leila, 35 — Being a lawyer was exciting at first, but I was working seventy-hour weeks and hardly saw my children. Teaching isn't easy either — the marking never stops — but my evenings are mine again. The hardest part was going back to university at thirty-two, surrounded by people ten years younger.

Dev, 29 — I'd always cooked for friends, and people kept telling me I should open a restaurant. I didn't take them seriously until I lost my job as an engineer. Now I run a small kitchen serving food from my grandmother's recipes. My parents still ask when I'm going to get a proper job, which hurts a little.

Anna, 52 — I loved nursing, but after a back injury I couldn't do the physical work any more. Painting had always been my hobby, so I took a course, and to my amazement my first exhibition sold out. I still volunteer at the hospital once a week — I couldn't give it up completely.

B 萊拉（35 歲）：當律師一開始很刺激，可是我一週工作七十小時，幾乎見不到孩子。教書也不輕鬆，改不完的作業，但我的晚上又屬於自己了。最難的是三十二歲回大學念書，身邊都是小我十歲的人。
C 戴夫（29 歲）：我一直都會做菜請朋友吃，大家老是說我應該開餐廳。直到我丟了工程師的工作，才當真。現在我經營一間小廚房，賣我奶奶食譜上的菜。我爸媽還是會問我什麼時候要找份正經工作，這讓我有點受傷。

衰退了幾十年後，夜車正在歐洲捲土重來。許多在意環境的旅客現在寧可不搭短程航班，臥鋪火車讓他們邊休息邊跨越長距離。業者推出有私人包廂的新車廂來回應需求。批評者指出，票價可能比機票貴，而且常常很慢。但支持者說這沒抓到重點：你省下了旅館錢，而且醒來就在市中心，而不是幾英里外的機場。夜車能否保持人氣，要看政府願不願意提供所需的投資。

Why we love lists
Most of us make lists of some kind, (9) ＿＿＿＿＿ it is shopping lists, to-do lists or lists of films we want to see. Psychologists say there is a good reason for this. When we have a lot to do, our brains find (10) ＿＿＿＿＿ hard to stop thinking about unfinished tasks. Writing them down seems to calm us, (11) ＿＿＿＿＿ we haven't actually done anything yet. Lists also give us a sense of achievement: few things are (12) ＿＿＿＿＿ satisfying as crossing an item off. (13) ＿＿＿＿＿ the other hand, a list that is too long can have the opposite effect. Experts suggest limiting a daily list to no (14) ＿＿＿＿＿ than five items, and putting the most difficult task first, (15) ＿＿＿＿＿ that it doesn't get pushed to the next day. After all, a list is only useful (16) ＿＿＿＿＿ it helps us act.

我們為什麼愛清單
大多數人都會列某種清單，不管是購物清單、待辦清單，還是想看的電影清單。心理學家說這有充分的理由。事情很多時，大腦很難停止去想未完成的工作。把它們寫下來似乎能讓我們平靜，即使我們其實還什麼都沒做。清單也給人成就感：很少有事比劃掉一項更令人滿足。另一方面，太長的清單可能適得其反。專家建議每天的清單不超過五項，並把最難的事放第一個，以免拖到隔天。畢竟，清單只有在幫助我們行動時才有用。

items.text:
My year as a lighthouse keeper's assistant
When I saw the advert for an assistant on a remote Scottish island, I almost didn't apply. I was twenty-three, I'd never lived outside a city, and the job description mentioned 'long periods of isolation' twice. But I was bored with my office job and wanted an adventure, so I sent off my CV, not really expecting a reply.
The island had no shop, no internet and a supply boat once a fortnight — when the weather allowed. My boss, Angus, had looked after the lighthouse for thirty years. He was a man of few words, and for the first month I thought he disliked me. Only later did I realise that he simply preferred showing to telling. He would fix something in silence, then hand me the tools the next time it broke.
The work itself was less romantic than I had imagined. The light was automatic, so our job was mainly maintenance: painting, checking the generator, recording the weather every three hours. What I hadn't expected was how much I would come to love the routine. Without a phone, I read more books in that year than in the previous five.
The hardest moment came in February, when a storm cut us off for five weeks. We ran short of fresh food, and I was genuinely frightened. Angus stayed calm, cooking surprisingly good meals from tins. When the boat finally arrived, I cried.
I've been back in the city for two years now. People ask if I was lonely. The honest answer is that I have felt lonelier in crowded offices than I ever did on that island.

tr.zh:
我當燈塔看守員助理的一年
看到蘇格蘭偏遠小島招助理的廣告時，我差點沒應徵。我二十三歲，從沒離開過城市，工作說明還兩次提到「長時間與世隔絕」。但我厭倦了辦公室工作，想冒險，就寄了履歷，沒真的期待回音。
島上沒有商店、沒有網路，補給船兩週來一次——天氣允許的話。我的上司安格斯看守燈塔三十年了。他話很少，頭一個月我以為他不喜歡我。後來才明白他只是喜歡做給人看，而不是說。他會默默修好東西，下次壞了就把工具遞給我。
工作本身沒有想像中浪漫。燈是自動的，我們主要做維護：油漆、檢查發電機、每三小時記錄天氣。我沒料到自己會那麼喜歡這種規律。沒有手機，那一年我讀的書比之前五年加起來還多。
最難熬的是二月，一場暴風雨讓我們與外界斷絕五週。新鮮食物不夠了，我真的很害怕。安格斯很冷靜，用罐頭做出出乎意料好吃的菜。補給船終於到的時候，我哭了。
我回城市已經兩年。大家問我會不會寂寞。老實說，我在擁擠的辦公室裡感到的寂寞，比在那座島上任何時候都多。

questions.q: Why did the writer nearly not apply for the job?
options: It seemed very different from his previous life.
He did not think he was qualified.
He was about to start a new job.
questions.zh: 二十三歲、沒離開過城市、說明強調與世隔絕：和過去的生活差太多。
questions.en: It was so unlike his city life.

questions.q: What did the writer later understand about Angus?
options: He was unhappy on the island.
He did not trust young people.
He taught by example rather than explanation.
questions.zh: 「他只是喜歡做給人看，而不是說」。

questions.q: What does the writer say about the work?
options: It was more exciting than he expected.
It mostly involved looking after equipment.
It required him to operate the light.
It left him no free time.
questions.zh: 「我們主要做維護」：油漆、檢查發電機、記錄天氣。

questions.q: What surprised the writer about life on the island?
options: He missed his phone very much.
He found it hard to concentrate on books.
questions.zh: 「我沒料到自己會那麼喜歡這種規律」。

questions.q: How did Angus behave during the storm?
questions.zh: 「安格斯很冷靜」。

questions.q: What is the writer's main point in the final paragraph?
options: City life is better than island life.
Being among people does not stop loneliness.
He would like to return to the island.
He was very lonely on the island.
questions.zh: 在擁擠辦公室比在島上更寂寞：人多不代表不孤單。

items.text:
Learning to swim as an adult
I was forty-one when I finally learned to swim. As a child I'd had a bad experience at a crowded pool, and after that I simply avoided water. (37) ＿＿＿＿＿
What changed my mind was my daughter. She was starting lessons and wanted me to come in with her. I didn't want to pass my fear on to her. (38) ＿＿＿＿＿
My instructor, Sam, began by asking me to do nothing more than stand in the shallow end. For the first three lessons, I didn't even put my face in the water. (39) ＿＿＿＿＿ By the fifth lesson I was floating on my back, which felt like a small miracle.
Progress wasn't steady, though. Some weeks I seemed to go backwards, and once I nearly gave up. (40) ＿＿＿＿＿ Sam reminded me that adults often learn more slowly because we think too much.
After six months, I swam a full length of the pool. (41) ＿＿＿＿＿ My daughter, who by then could swim much better than me, was waiting at the other end, clapping.
Now I swim twice a week. (42) ＿＿＿＿＿ If you've always been afraid, it's never too late to start.
bank: It didn't sound like much, but it was exactly what I needed.
I told everyone that I simply didn't enjoy swimming.
It was only twenty-five metres, but I felt as if I'd crossed an ocean.
So I booked a course of private lessons at our local pool.
That was when I discovered I was actually a natural swimmer.
It isn't fast or elegant, but it's mine.
What kept me going was the thought of my daughter's face.
The pool was closed for repairs for most of the summer.

tr.zh:
成年後學游泳
我四十一歲才終於學會游泳。小時候在擁擠的泳池有過不好的經驗，之後我就乾脆避開水。我跟大家說我只是不喜歡游泳。
讓我改變心意的是女兒。她要開始上課，想要我陪她下水。我不想把恐懼傳給她。所以我在附近泳池報名了私人課程。
教練山姆一開始只要我站在淺水區，前三堂課我連臉都沒放進水裡。聽起來沒什麼，但正是我需要的。到第五堂課，我已經能仰漂，感覺像小小的奇蹟。
不過進步不是一路順利。有幾週我好像在退步，有一次差點放棄。讓我撐下去的是想到女兒的表情。山姆提醒我，大人學得慢，常是因為想太多。
六個月後，我游完整整一趟泳池。只有二十五公尺，我卻覺得像橫渡了大海。那時女兒已經游得比我好多了，在另一端等我、為我鼓掌。
現在我每週游兩次。不快也不優雅，但那是我自己的。如果你一直都怕水，開始永遠不嫌晚。

questions.zh: 避開水，並且對大家說「只是不喜歡游泳」。
不想把恐懼傳給女兒，「所以」報名課程；下一段接著說教練。
只站在淺水區、不放臉：「聽起來沒什麼，但正是我需要的」。
差點放棄，「讓我撐下去的是女兒」。
游完一趟泳池：「只有二十五公尺」。
每週游兩次：「不快也不優雅，但那是我自己的」。

bank: Priya, 29 — I became a volunteer firefighter in my village three years ago. The training took six months of evenings and weekends, and I nearly quit during the physical tests. Now I carry a pager and can be called out at any time, even in the middle of the night. My employer lets me leave work for emergencies, which I'm very grateful for.

Tom, 52 — I've volunteered at a food bank every Saturday for ten years. It started because a friend needed help with driving the van, and I never stopped. The people who come in are often embarrassed, so I try to make them feel welcome. It's changed how I think about my own spending.

Elena, 19 — I spent last summer volunteering at a sea turtle centre in Greece. I paid for my own flights, which was a lot of money for a student. The work was hard — night patrols on the beach to protect nests — but seeing the baby turtles reach the sea made it all worthwhile. I'm now studying marine biology.

Jamal, 34 — I read to children at our local hospital twice a month. I'm not a teacher, and at first I worried the kids would find me boring. Actually, they correct me when I get stories wrong! It's the most relaxing part of my week, completely different from my job in finance.

tr.zh:
A 普莉雅，29 歲：三年前我在村子當義消。訓練花了六個月的晚上和週末，體能測驗時差點放棄。現在我帶著呼叫器，隨時可能被叫出勤，連半夜也是。我的老闆讓我有緊急狀況時離開工作，我很感激。
B 湯姆，52 歲：我十年來每週六在食物銀行當志工。一開始是朋友需要人幫忙開貨車，後來我就沒停過。來的人常覺得難為情，所以我盡量讓他們感到受歡迎。這改變了我對自己花錢的看法。
C 艾蓮娜，19 歲：去年暑假我在希臘的海龜中心當志工。機票自己付，對學生來說是一大筆錢。工作很辛苦，晚上在海灘巡邏保護巢穴，但看到小海龜爬進海裡，一切都值得了。我現在讀海洋生物。
D 賈馬爾，34 歲：我每個月兩次到本地醫院唸故事給小朋友聽。我不是老師，一開始擔心孩子覺得我很無聊。結果我故事講錯時他們還會糾正我！這是我一週最放鬆的時光，和我在金融業的工作完全不同。
